projections.note: What a leaderboard row is. Every field here is public, which is the point: an entry that carried one narrower field would be a shape the server has to redact per viewer, and a redaction that fails open publishes it.
The four fields that never leave the participant's own surface. This shape exists so that the narrowing is a schema boundary rather than a per-field redaction on a public shape.

fields.name: token_burn_total
fields.reason: D-144. Published beside credited_token_burn it yields the composite weight by division, and since evidence_class is already public that yields the trust factor and therefore the sanction D-084 keeps private.

fields.name: confidence_weight_hundredths
fields.reason: The composite ADR-020 weight. Publishing it is publishing the sanction directly rather than by division.

fields.name: evidence_factor_hundredths
fields.reason: One of the two factors. Public alone it would let the trust factor be recovered from the composite.

fields.name: trust_factor_hundredths
fields.reason: The ranked-identity trust state expressed as a number. It is the sanction.

fields.name: recent_credited_token_burn
fields.reason: A short-window series. Differencing it against the published credited figure recovers the weight over that window.

fields.name: trust_notice_id
fields.reason: D-227 records the limit it works around: the ranked-identity states ADR-020 reads are marked internal, so a participant reaches their own trust state as a notice reference rather than by name.

projections.note: Served only after the current-viewer-authorization profile admits the viewer. Public here means public-once-authorized, and the authorization is the D-386 rule rather than a property of this shape.
The participant's own account. `admitted` is a boolean rather than a lifecycle under D-288, because the account is told none of the five invite states.

fields.name: visibility
fields.reason: A viewer who could read the setting could tell a private profile from one they are merely not authorized for, which is the distinction privacy exists to remove.

fields.name: admitted
fields.reason: D-288. It renders the redemption screen without provoking a 403, and it says nothing to anyone else about the size or membership of the invite ring.

fields.name: revision
fields.reason: A concurrency token for the participant's own conditional updates; it has no meaning to a third party.

projections.note: An accepted claim as its own submitter sees it. No claim is ever public: the binding rules admit only fixed-schema aggregate accounting across the device boundary, and a per-claim record on a public surface would be an activity timeline.

fields.name: claim_id
fields.reason: Names one submission by one device at one time.

fields.name: device_id
fields.reason: Which of the participant's machines was working.

fields.name: sequence
fields.reason: The lineage position; a sequence disclosed publicly is a count of the participant's sessions.

fields.name: state
fields.reason: A retracted or quarantined claim is an integrity outcome, which D-084 keeps private to the participant.

fields.name: evidence_class
fields.reason: Public in aggregate on the profile; per claim it would let an observer locate the exact submission that changed a participant's class.

fields.name: payload_digest
fields.reason: Bound to one claim, so it is an identifier for a submission even though the digest itself discloses nothing.

fields.name: appraisal_id
fields.reason: Names the verifier appraisal, which is integrity-private.

fields.name: accepted_at
fields.reason: An exact acceptance time is a working-hours signal at a resolution the presence projection deliberately does not offer.

projections.note: The verifier appraisal of one of the participant's own claims, as the participant sees it. No appraisal is ever public and none is ever authorized to a viewer: the identifier that reaches it is itself `self` on ClaimRecord, and the record is integrity-private. This shape is a projection rather than the stored record because two of the record's fields are withheld from the participant too — `evaluated.anomaly_disposition`, whose `under-review` and `shadow-only` values are the statement D-381 keeps from them that a case is open, and `policy.implementation_sha256`, the verifier's own build digest. Neither appears in this shape at all, so their absence is uniform and is not itself a signal. What remains is the effect on the participant's standing, which D-084 requires be told to them.

fields.name: appraisal_id
fields.reason: Names one appraisal of one submission. It is reachable only from ClaimRecord.appraisal_id, which is self.

fields.name: claim_id
fields.reason: The submission appraised. Same audience as the claim itself, which is self in every field.

fields.name: canonical_claim_sha256
fields.reason: Bound to one claim, so it identifies a submission even though the digest discloses nothing on its own.

fields.name: evidence_bundle_sha256
fields.reason: Identifies the device-local bundle that explains the claim. Null when the device retained none, which is an input to the capture dimension rather than a neutral absence.

fields.name: policy
fields.reason: The published policy bundle and its content digest. The verifier build digest the record also carries is not in this shape: it is not the participant's personal data and no appeal needs it.

fields.name: authority
fields.reason: A constant. It records that the server verifier decided, which is what stops a surface presenting the outcome as client-selected.

fields.name: client_influence
fields.reason: A constant. Present so a client that renders the appraisal cannot imply it requested any part of it.

fields.name: attestation
fields.reason: Three constants recording D-100: the appraisal assesses a self-report and is never a provider confirmation. Omitting them is what would invite the misreading.

fields.name: acceptance_outcome
fields.reason: The outcome for this claim. D-084 requires the affected participant be told the effect; it is silent toward everyone else.

fields.name: dimensions
fields.reason: The seven evidence dimensions. The participant already reads the derived ADR-020 factors on SelfRankEntry, so this discloses strictly less to them than what they hold, and it discloses nothing to anyone else.

fields.name: evaluated
fields.reason: Which rule bundles, certification bundle, accounting profile and equivalence rule were applied. This is what an appeal argues against, so withholding it would leave the appeal route D-084 promises unusable.

fields.name: awarded_profile_id
fields.reason: The internal profile identifier. It stays internal: the API's public vocabulary is evidence_class, and this field is here for the participant's own appeal rather than for any surface.

fields.name: evidence_class
fields.reason: The record's public_state under D-143. Public in aggregate on the profile; per appraisal it would locate the exact submission that changed a participant's class, which is the same reason ClaimRecord.evidence_class is self.

fields.name: ranking_eligibility
fields.reason: Whether this claim competes. quarantined and retracted are integrity outcomes, which D-084 keeps private to the participant.

fields.name: reason_codes
fields.reason: A closed vocabulary from reason-codes-v1.json, whose appealability column is how the participant learns whether the outcome can be appealed.

fields.name: validity
fields.reason: When this appraisal applied. Bound to one participant's claim and meaningless to a third party.

fields.name: supersession
fields.reason: The append-only correction chain. A re-evaluation is a new appraisal rather than an edit, and the trigger names why the verifier looked again.

projections.note: The projection, never the lease. `availability` is the three-value collapse the binding table declares; the underlying five-state lease, the device and the generation stay server-side.
A closed-world typed event. There is no free-text field and no payload, which is what makes it impossible for a notification to carry source-derived content.

fields.name: notification_id
fields.reason: Addresses one row in one participant's inbox.

fields.name: type
fields.reason: The event class; it is the participant's own inbox and nobody else's.

fields.name: actor_account_id
fields.reason: Who caused it. Disclosed to the recipient only, and rechecked at delivery time under D-386 in case the actor was blocked after the row was created.

fields.name: scope_id
fields.reason: The board, generation or case the event is about.

fields.name: state
fields.reason: Includes retracted, which is a correction to this recipient and to nobody else.

fields.name: created_at
fields.reason: The recipient's own inbox timeline.

fields.name: delivered_at
fields.reason: When the item reached the server inbox. Server-assigned because no transport may set it: a push acceptance is a hint about this item and never evidence that it arrived.

fields.name: group_count
fields.reason: How many source events this one item stands for. It is a count over the recipient's own events and names none of them.

fields.name: read_at
fields.reason: When the recipient marked it read. It is the recipient's own act, disclosed to nobody else, and no transport acknowledgement can produce it.

fields.name: retracted_at
fields.reason: When the product withdrew the item. A correction to this recipient and to nobody else.

fields.name: retraction_reason_code
fields.reason: Why it was withdrawn, from the reason registry. A closed vocabulary, so a retraction cannot smuggle free text into an inbox that has no free-text field.

projections.note: What one of the participant's own devices did with one deletion command. It is self-only in every field: a deletion is not a social event, and the set of devices a person enrolled is integrity data that no viewer, board administrator or other participant may read. Nothing here names a path, a project, a repository or a file, because a deletion receipt that had to say what it deleted would have to carry the thing the privacy boundary forbids crossing it.

fields.name: device_id
fields.reason: Which of the participant's devices. Disclosed to the participant only.

fields.name: disposition
fields.reason: The per-device answer D-076 requires. Derived from the command row and never selected by the device or the client.

fields.name: issued_at
fields.reason: When the command was written.

fields.name: expires_at
fields.reason: When an unanswered command stops waiting. It is what makes unreachable a bounded answer rather than an indefinite one.

fields.name: receipt_received_at
fields.reason: When the device's signed receipt arrived. Absent when none did, which is the normal case and is reported as such.

fields.name: residual_risk
fields.reason: What the device could not rule out. Present only with a receipt, never inferred from its absence, and its strongest value says observed rather than none.
